- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to avoid underreaction.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes — apply lagged smoothing: reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 periods after a spike.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit recent trends; apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward 30-day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) and price remains stable, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals — adjust forecast downward if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 5 days.
